title: PES - Pandemic Emergency Scenario
description: This dataset contains EEG and behavioural data from 9 participants performing a complex decision-making task simulating a pandemic emergency resource-allocation scenario. Participants, paired with an artificial agent, allocated resources across 64 sequences while EEG, ECG, and EOG signals were recorded, along with their subjective confidence in each decision. The dataset is intended to support research into neurophysiological correlates of strategic decision-making under uncertainty.
methods_description: Each participant wore a 64-channel Biosemi ActiveTwo EEG system with wet electrodes placed according to the International 10-20 System, plus 8 additional external channels (2 ECG, 4 EOG). EEG data were sampled at 2048 Hz. Participants sat about 1 meter from an LCD monitor and performed resource-allocation decisions using mouse press, drag, and release actions, followed by a confidence report via mouse wheel movement.
